To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the iodination of the thioether group is catalyzed by phosphate ion, whereas the oxidation reaction is not; and that the iodination and oxidation reactions are strongly catalysed by hydroxide ion, whereas the iodination is catalyzed more strongly.

the rate of the iodination of the phenolic moiety in tyrosine-containing biomolecules can be greatly accelerated by raising the pH and by increasing the concentration of phosphate ions, whereas the rate of oxidation of sulfur-containing residues is unaffected by these conditions.
iodination of the thioether group of biomolecules is catalyzed by phosphate ion, whereas iodination of the phenolic group is catalyzed both by hydroxide ion and by phosphate ion.

the kinetics of reactions between iodine(3) and amino acids and small peptide molecules.
the development of a method for radioiodination of biomolecular tyrosine residues in the presence of sulfur-containing residues.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the iodination of biomolecules in phosphate buffer at pH greater than 7.5 is a useful method for selectively iodinating tyrosine-containing biomolecules, provided that the biomolecule contains no thiol or thioether groups.

iodination of biomolecules with I-(3) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer at a pH above 7.0 would give high yield of iodination of tyrosine residues with little oxidative damage to the sulfur-containing residues.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the iodination of tyrosine residues in oxidation-sensitive biomolecules can be carried out in the pH range from 7.5 to 8.5, in the absence of a reducing agent, and with minimal oxidation of the sulfur functionality.
